Implementation split filed (this design carries no implementation work itself):

- Watchdog core — #6032 (disk state, failure classes, repair ladder, adapter loader, producer scaffolding)
- Escalation mechanism — #6033 (fleet queue task + deduplicated incident issue, auto-close on recovery, human-blocked surfacing)
- Mistral adapter #1 — [openchamber#1630](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/issues/1630) (**blocked** on the Mistral sign-in lane's data-path outcome: Vibe token usage API vs console endpoint + cookie)

Design note: `~/workspace/scratch/mistral-quota-watchdog-2026-11-04/design.md`. Umbrella: #1260 (noted there). Companion reads: #5928, #4889, [openchamber#1619](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/issues/1619).

## Triage findings (verified fresh this shift)

- Issue #6031 is OPEN, no hard-stop labels (`held`, `user/owned`, `do-not-merge`, `do-not-auto-edit` all absent), carrying Drew's 2026-11-04 directive verbatim and a complete design (three parts on the laptop, health/failure-class model, repair ladder, disk state per issue #5928's lesson, alerting posture). No packet defect — this is one of the best-specified design packets in the current batch.
- **Acceptance item 2 (implementation issues exist with their own criteria): MET, verified.** Issue #6032 (watchdog core: disk state, failure classes, repair ladder, adapter loader, producer scaffolding) and issue #6033 (escalation: fleet queue task + deduplicated incident issue, auto-close on recovery, human-blocked surfacing) are both OPEN in this repo; the Mistral adapter is openchamber#1630, OPEN and explicitly blocked on the Mistral sign-in lane's data-path outcome (Vibe token usage API vs console endpoint + cookie) — that blocker is recorded on both issues, not discovered here.
- **Acceptance item 3 (catalogue reflected in issue #1260): MET per the filer's note** — the split comment on this issue records "Umbrella: #1260 (noted there)", and issue #1260 is OPEN as the SLO/self-healing umbrella this design specializes.
- **Acceptance item 1 (open questions answered or explicitly deferred): dispositioned here, explicitly deferred with defaults.** (Q1) Escalation-unresolved NEEDS DREW threshold: proposed 24 h stands as the working default — it only tunes alerting, and the design already marks it non-blocking. (Q2) Human-blocked recovery stays silent with the closed incident issue as the record: stands as proposed. (Q3) Producer source home (`pm-stack/exporters/` here vs beside the quota module in openchamber): deferred to the claim of issue #6032 with the design's own proposal (`pm-stack/exporters/` in this repo, beside the gatherer's FILE_EXPORTS machinery it feeds) as the default — the decision is cheap to reverse before code lands and should not gate the core's start. None of the three needs Drew unless he wants to override a default; if he does, this comment is the place it will be noticed.
- **Ordering:** issue #6032 (core) is the start; issue #6033 (escalation) is ladder step 4 and can follow or parallel once the core's failure-class contract is fixed; openchamber#1630 waits on its named sign-in blocker, not on this design. No follow-up packet enqueued — the implementation work already has its own issues and will be claimed through them.

## Triage verdict: REAL AND CURRENT — remainder returned to the queue

Queue task 12448 (lane `ec118cad-0fd3-4652-91c4-27432f2f2efd`), re-triaged under Drew's triage doctrine (2026-11-07, #7016) because task 10397 marked this done with no landed evidence.

**Verified fresh (2026-11-08T06:50Z):**

- #6031 OPEN, no hard-stop labels. The design body still carries Drew's 2026-11-04 directive and the three-part shape (producer / watchdog core / gatherer).
- Split issues both still OPEN: **#6032** (watchdog core — disk state, failure classes, repair ladder) and **#6033** (escalation — fleet queue task + deduplicated incident issue).
- Umbrella **#1260** OPEN.
- Prior triage's acceptance findings re-checked and still hold: implementation issues exist with their own criteria, the umbrella is noted, and the three open questions are dispositioned with defaults (Q1 24 h escalation threshold, Q2 silent human-blocked recovery, Q3 producer home deferred to #6032's claim with `pm-stack/exporters/` as the default).

**What was missing — the reason this returns to the queue:** no queue packet existed for #6032 or #6033 in any status, and no implementation exists (`pm-stack/` has `meta-exporter` and `opencode-usage-export` but no `exporters/` or watchdog module). Triage had annotated the design but never put the work in front of a worker.

**Action taken:** enqueued **task 13006** (`repo-health:v1:fix:developing-today/code:issue:6032`) scoped to the watchdog core per the design's own ordering — the core first, escalation (#6033) after its failure-class contract is fixed. `pm-stack/exporters/` is taken as Q3's default, and the timers must land in `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` per AGENTS.md.

#6031 stays OPEN as the design record until its splits land, as the prior triage recorded.
